title: Introduce latency-cushion admission and regional fallback orchestrator
author: Lena Chen
description: Context: During a recent multi-region incident we observed bursty latency tails that caused aggressive load-shedding to kick in too early for small cohorts. This PR introduces a lightweight "latency cushion" admission policy plus a regional fallback orchestrator that coordinates staged drains and accelerated KV-preserve handoffs across candidate regions. Goal: reduce unnecessary tenant evictions and avoid cascading regional failovers while preserving SLOs under transient latency tail events. This change is targeted at the serving runtime and the control plane routing logic; it is backward-compatible and feature-flagged.
commit_summary: 4 commits: 1) add latency_cushion admission policy and config; 2) implement cushion-aware dispatcher routing; 3) regional fallback orchestrator and probe protocol; 4) telemetry, unit tests and docs. Commits include interface stubs for feature-flag gating and an emergency revert patch in case of regression.
changed_files: High-level files changed: runtime/admission/latency_cushion.go (+430 -22), routing/orchestrator/fallback_coordinator.go (+210 -9), routing/orchestrator/probe_protocol.go (+84 -4), telemetry/metrics_registry.go (+72 -18), controlplane/flags/feature_flags.go (+6 -2), docs/operations/latency-cushion.md (+35 -0), tests/* (unit + integration harness updates). No schema or API surface changes exposed to customers.
design_details: Latency cushion: per-tenant adaptive cushion computed from observed p95/p99 baseline and recent tail excursions. Admission policy categorizes incoming requests as immediate/admit-with-cushion/evict. 'Admit-with-cushion' allows a short additional wait window (configurable, default 150ms) where we accept the request but mark it as cushion-tracked; the request participates in KV-preserve fastpath and receives priority in KV cache reuse. Cushion windows are bounded and decay per-tenant to avoid long-lived exemptions. Regional fallback orchestrator: a control-plane coordinator that, when triggered by sustained regional KV pressure or probe failures, sequences candidate failover steps: mark-sticky-quiet -> staged drain -> prefetch target slot -> expedited KV-snapshot -> atomic switch. Orchestrator integrates with existing rollout and canary logic; it includes a probe protocol with exponential backoff and jitter. Feature flags: Safe rollout behind flags: runtime.latency_cushion.enabled and routing.fallback_orchestrator.v1.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests: 42 new cases covering cushion state machine, decay, and eviction edge cases. Integration: added a synthetic burst scenario to perf-canary harness simulating p99 spikes across 50 tenants to validate no regression in median latency and SLO preservation. Load tests: 1h soak in benchmark-lab showed 6-8% reduction in tenant evictions during transient tails with <1% change in p50/p90. Telemetry: new metrics registered: runtime.latency_cushion.admits, runtime.latency_cushion.evictions_saved, orchestrator.step_durations, orchestrator.probe_failures. Added tags for tenant_id and region to facilitate incident triage.
rollback_and_mitigation: Rollback plan: feature flags allow immediate disable. Emergency revert commit included (revert feature flag initialization and orchestrator registration). Runbook: SRE runbook updated with steps to globally disable runtime.latency_cushion.enabled and routing.fallback_orchestrator.v1 via controlplane toggle + restart-less config push. If observing increased p99 or KV pressure, revert orchestrator and disable cushion.
review_conversation: Arun Gupta: asked for clearer bounds on cushion decay and vector attack surface (malicious clients sustaining cushion). Response (Lena): added per-tenant credit tank with max tokens and observable depletion metric; updated tests. Morgan Lee: requested telemetry to separate 'saved eviction' events from 'soft-admit' timeouts — implemented in commit 3. Tara Singh (SRE): requested an emergency disable path and explicit knob in the health dashboard; added flag + dashboard patch. Final: approvals from Arun and Tara after a CI rerun. Morgan gave LGTM for telemetry clarity.
ci_checks: CI pipeline: lint -> unit tests -> integration (perf-canary emulator) -> e2e smoke. First run: unit failure (race in cushion state machine) detected; fixed by atomic state update and retry backoff. Second run: all checks green. Perf-canary reported expected eviction reduction; nightly stability run scheduled.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-03-05 by Lena Chen after approvals. Merge notes: enabled feature flags default to off; rollout schedule: staged enable for non-production regions for 48h, then progressive enable in canary tenants, and finally global opt-in. Added release note entry for ops and SDK teams.
release_notes:
- Introduced 'latency cushion' admission policy to reduce premature tenant evictions during transient tail spikes (feature-flagged).
- Added Regional Fallback Orchestrator to coordinate staged drains with KV-preserve handoff (feature-flagged).
- New telemetry: runtime.latency_cushion.admits, runtime.latency_cushion.evictions_saved, orchestrator.step_durations.
- Rollout is gated via runtime.latency_cushion.enabled and routing.fallback_orchestrator.v1 flags. Ops: follow updated runbook if enabling.
notes_for_release_manager: Coordinate with Dedicated on a canary window because the orchestrator changes routing semantics during staged drains. Notify customer-facing incident team and update support playbooks with new flag names.
